subject: Dedicated capacity: follow-up on pricing & throughput targets
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@hyperionai.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity: follow-up on pricing & throughput targets

Hi Samira —

Great to meet today, thanks for walking us through HyperionAI's inference profile. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned: 

Recap from the call:
- Workload: mostly chat/completion use cases with some short-form summarization. Typical prompt+response median length ~600 tokens; 95th percentile session ~1,800 tokens.
- Volume: currently ~45M tokens/month baseline with peaks up to ~120M tokens/month. Your internal forecast is 200–300M tokens/month in 12 months with steady growth.
- Throughput target: target P95 response latency <400ms for short responses; want sustained throughput of ~350 concurrent generation streams (roughly 60–80 requests/s depending on response length).
- Preferred GPU: you mentioned H100 for latency-sensitive production, willing to consider A100 for non-critical workloads.
- Budget target: your procurement team indicated target blended cost ~ $600–1,200 per 1M tokens (ballpark), with flexibility depending on reserved commitment and support SLAs.

Questions we raised that would help us firm pricing:
1) Can you confirm average tokens per request (prompt+response) and % of requests that hit the 95th percentile length?
2) Any hard constraints on latency for peak traffic windows?
3) Are you open to a mixed pool (e.g., H100 for 60% reserved capacity, A100 for burst)?

Proposed next steps:
- I'll pull together a Dedicated capacity sketch with two sizing options (H100-heavy and mixed H100/A100), estimated reserved GPU count, and modeled cost per 1M tokens at your forecasted volumes.
- Could you share the Q1 usage snapshot you mentioned (short CSV) so we can run a quick unit-economics model?
- If the sketch looks good, we can move to a short-term pilot (4–8 weeks) to validate latencies and effective throughput.

I've attached a draft pricing matrix and a usage snapshot template. Happy to hop on another 30-min call if helpful.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0147

Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: follow-up on pricing & throughput targets

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap — this looks right to me. Quick clarifications:
- Avg tokens/request: ~420 tokens (prompt ~120, response ~300)
- Hot path (approx 15% of traffic) is the longer sessions that reach ~1,500–1,800 tokens.
- Latency constraint: P95 target for hot path is 600ms, short responses should be under 350–400ms.
- We are definitely open to a mixed pool approach — prefer H100 for the hot path and A100 for standard loads if the unit economics make sense.

I've attached the Q1 usage CSV (exported anonymized). Couple more notes: procurement wants a target unit cost under $900/1M tokens to move forward quickly; they'll consider $900–1,200 if we can show measurable tail-latency improvements and an SLA.

I'll review the draft pricing matrix and follow up by EOD tomorrow.

—Samira

Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity: follow-up on pricing & throughput targets 

Marcus / Rishi —

Looping you both in to get a quick sizing + pricing sketch ready for Hyperion. Key asks from the customer:
- Target blended unit cost: ideally <= $900/1M tokens; acceptable up to $1,200 if we provide H100 tail-latency guarantees and a short pilot.
- Forecast: 200–300M tokens/month in 12 months (they're at ~45M now).
- Throughput: sustained ~350 concurrent streams; P95 latency targets noted in Samira's reply.

I'm attaching the draft matrix Samira will review. Can you propose two SKU sketches:
A) H100-dominant reserved pool (specify GPU count, expected sustained throughput, modeled $/1M tokens at 200M and 300M tokens/month)
B) Mixed pool (H100 for hot path ~60% capacity, A100 for baseline ~40%) with same metrics.

Also note procurement emphasis on predictable pricing and PO timeline — they want a simple reserved capacity number to include in the budget.

Can you get something short today? Samira said procurement wants a decision quickly.

Thanks,
Marissa
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 18:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated capacity: follow-up on pricing & throughput targets

Marissa / Rishi —

Sketch below — quick assumptions: inference model footprint aligns with 70B-class model performance; avg token compute cost calibrated to our internal A100/H100 perf curves; KV cache hit-rate ~20% for their workloads (helps unit economics). Numbers are coarse but should be defensible for procurement.

Option A — H100-dominant (recommended for latency):
- Reserved pool: 10 H100 GPUs (rented as dedicated nodes)
- Expected sustained throughput: ~120–140M tokens/day (~3.5–4.5M tokens/hour) at tail-latency P95 <400ms for short responses; supports ~350 concurrent short streams with headroom for hot path.
- Modeled cost per 1M tokens:
  - At 200M tokens/month: ~$820/1M tokens
  - At 300M tokens/month: ~$650/1M tokens
- Notes: H100 gives ~30–40% lower latency vs A100 on these workloads. Needs ~1.2x reserved capacity buffer for predictable tail-latency during peaks.

Option B — Mixed H100/A100 (cost-optimized):
- Reserved pool: 6 H100 + 6 A100 (mixed pool; H100 handles hot path)
- Expected sustained throughput: ~100–130M tokens/day aggregated; slightly higher latency tail for hot path but generally within 600ms P95 for long sessions.
- Modeled cost per 1M tokens:
  - At 200M tokens/month: ~$680/1M tokens
  - At 300M tokens/month: ~$540/1M tokens
- Notes: Mixed approach lowers blended unit cost by ~15–20% vs H100-only but requires routing policy + fallback to ensure hot path hits H100.

Pilot recommendation:
- 4–8 week pilot with 4 H100 + 4 A100 to validate tail-latency and actual token throughput. Use autoscale + burst credits for short peaks.
- Deliverable: pilot SLOs (latency/availability) and measured $/1M tokens. If pilot validates, convert to reserved commit (e.g., 10 H100 or mixed 6+6).

Next steps I suggest:
1) Share these two sketches with Samira/procurement; ask for fast feedback on the 10 H100 vs mixed 6+6 tradeoff.
2) If they accept pilot, we prepare a simple PO + short pilot contract (30–60 day billing) and schedule a technical onboarding slot with infra@hyperionai.

Happy to jump on a call to walk through the numbers with Samira.

—Marcus
Sr Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
